Swaroop Mishra
Swaroop Mishra is an Indian research scientist recognized for his contributions to the field of artificial intelligence, particularly in the development of large language models. He gained prominence as a Research Scientist at Google DeepMind, where he was involved in the creation of Gemini, a significant language model.
Mishra has consistently been engaged in the complete lifecycle of various language models and artificial intelligence tools. His expertise and contributions were further highlighted by his involvement in a system that achieved notable success at the International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO) 2024. As part of a team that included AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry, Mishra's work contributed to their winning of a silver medal at the prestigious competition. This achievement underscores the application of advanced AI techniques to complex mathematical problem-solving.
Early life and Education
Swaroop Mishra was born in Bhanjanagar, Ganjam, Odisha. His primary education commenced at Saraswati Shishu Vidya Mandir, Bhanjanagar, where he completed his secondary schooling in the academic year 2006-2007. In 2007, Mr. Mishra achieved a distinguished ranking within the top ten students of Odisha, specifically placing himself within the top seven students. This accomplishment was formally recognized by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Naveen Patnaik, who presented him with an award for his hard work and talent.
Mishra pursued his intermediate education at Buxi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar College, Bhubaneswar. Subsequently, he obtained his Bachelor's degree from Silicon University, Bhubaneswar, graduating in the class of 2014. Swaroop Mishra holds a Master of Technology (M.Tech.) degree from the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur), specializing in control and automation.He earned a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) from Arizona State University, with a focus on Artificial Intelligence.
Research and Career
''Swaroop's work is primarily focused on Large Language Models and Artificial Intelligence, particularly in areas like instruction tuning, prompting and AI self-improvement. But over the span of last 15 years, his research revolved around various topics related to Artificial Intelligence. His research has been published in top AI research papers and highlighted in conferences. Mishra's research includes:-
2009-2012: Unified Theory in Physics, String Theory
* 2011: (Library and Computer Center Access) Institute of Physics Bhubaneswar
* 2012: (Research Intern) Harish-Chandra Research Institute, Prayagraj
2012-2014: Efficient Energy Conversion and Generation
* 2013: (Research Intern): Research, Technology and Innovation Centre, Thermax, Pune
* 2014: (Summer Intern): Intelligent Systems & Control Lab, IIT Kanpur
2014-2016: Neural Networks, Cyber Physical Systems, Smart Grid and Machine Learning
* 2014-2016: Teaching Assistant, IIT Kanpur
2016-2018: Deep Learning Toolbox, Simulink, User-friendly Applications, Machine Learning ,App Development , Big Data
* 2016-2018: Software Engineer, Control, Design and Automation Group at MathWorks
2018-2019: Deep Learning, Computer Vision, Agentic App Development, Resource Allocation
* 2018-2019: Technical Consultant, Information Technology Research Academy, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India
2019-2023: Artificial Intelligence, Language Model, Natural Language Processing, Machine Learning, Instruction Tuning, Reasoning
* 2019-2023: Research Assistant, Arizona State University
* 2020-2022: Research Intern and Collaborator: Allen Institute for AI
* 2022: Research Intern, Microsoft Research
* 2022: Research Intern, Google Brain
2023-Now: Gemini, Superhuman Reasoning
* 2023-Now: Research Scientist, Google Brain and later Google DeepMind
Swaroop's'' journey, marked by a commitment to excellence and a breadth of experience, has established him as a key contributor to AI, effectively translating academic advancements into practical solutions.In essence, Swaroop Mishra is a leading researcher in the field of AI, particularly in the advancement of Large language Models and their reasoning capabilities.
